hits.excerpt: Chapter 50 Choosing repeated actions A repeated servicing decision changes both cash flows and the information available for later decisions. Choosing software therefore begins with the policy question: evaluate a fixed rule from logged experience, learn a rule and evaluate it separately, or plan within a supplied model. A numerical answer can be accurate for one of these questions and misleading for another. The chapter first examines learned policies and their evaluation populations, then R methods for learning and evaluating dynamic rules. The detailed Python comparisons distinguish sequential scores, one-time offers and hidden-state planning before bringing those choices together. Java and C++ provide contrasting learning, inference and planning implementations. The final Julia studies connect interface semantics to concrete model evaluation and partial- history weighting. Their worked examples keep policy selection, information loss, monetary scaling and uncertainty visible throughout. 50.1 d3rlpy: learning a policy without losing its evaluation target A collections team wants to choose the next contact, restructuring offer or referral from a borrower’s history. A library that learns actions from logged episodes is an attractive challenger to a manually specified rule. The proposal must nevertheless say which policy is evaluated, whose starting states define value, when money is received, and which unobserved

licy returns that an ordinary logged-only bank request cannot supply. These restrictions survive this comparison. OBP’s one-sided bound has a different contract, and its replay and tuning limitations require their own checks. The POMDP-Py review in Section 50.5.3 likewise withholds an exact-backend claim until the competing horizon recurrences and the belief and clock conversions are resolved. A common wrapper must preserve these different refusal reasons. OBP and SCOPE-RL declare Apache 2.0 licenses in the inspected roots; d3rlpy and POMDP-Py have inspected MIT declarations. Full dependency, data, compiler and distribution obligations remain specific to the chosen artifacts. POMDP-Py’s Cython components require native-binary and ABI custody; Python packaging alone does not remove that duty. The existing conversion contracts explain why a wholesale cross-language port would duplicate scientific, numerical and maintenance responsibilities without an established benefit. Small independent oracles remain valuable because they can expose semantic disagreement without inheriting the same implementation. (Yuta Saito and Open Bandit Pipeline contributors, 2022; Haruka Kiyohara and SCOPE-RL contributors, 2023;

hits.excerpt: emain explicit obligations. (Causal banking proposal project, 2026eg) Across the chapter, a useful comparison preserves the decision before comparing algorithms. A fitted controller, a value under a supplied model, an estimate from logged actions and a stationary population value answer different questions. The source-specific counterexamples show why state sufficiency, policy randomness, episode endings, support and reward clocks must survive conversion. The preferred route is consequently narrow reuse with explicit qualification and independent finite references; neither a language change nor a more elaborate optimizer supplies missing causal information. The next chapter turns to comparisons across institutions and time, where assignment, shared shocks and the choice of comparison group impose a different set of requirements.
